Run the ready-made CPU image with Docker, or follow the source-build
instructions below for a custom CPU or GPU build.

::: {.feature-opalx}
## Run with Docker {#run-with-docker}

The public image `ghcr.io/opalx-project/opalx:cpu` contains OPALX and its
runtime dependencies, including MPI. You do not need compilers or a local MPI
installation. It uses the CPU/OpenMP backend; GPU images are not provided.
Docker automatically selects the Linux x86-64 (`amd64`) or ARM64 image for
your machine, including Intel and Apple silicon Macs.

### Set up Docker on a Mac

1. Install [Docker Desktop for Mac](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/mac-install/),
   choosing the Apple silicon or Intel download to match your Mac.
2. Open Docker Desktop and wait until it is running.
3. In Terminal, check Docker and download the OPALX image:

```bash
docker run --rm hello-world
docker pull ghcr.io/opalx-project/opalx:cpu
docker run --rm ghcr.io/opalx-project/opalx:cpu --help
```

The public image can be pulled without a GitHub account or `docker login`.
Docker Desktop runs the Linux container on macOS. Allocate enough memory and
CPUs in Docker Desktop for your simulation.

Check that the image matches your Mac:

```bash
docker run --rm --entrypoint uname ghcr.io/opalx-project/opalx:cpu -m
```

Expect `aarch64` on Apple silicon and `x86_64` on Intel. If an Apple silicon
Mac reports `x86_64`, check whether `DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM` is set to
`linux/amd64`; this selects an Intel image that runs under slower emulation.
Unset that variable with `unset DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM`, then pull the image
again to select the native architecture.

### Run a first example {#docker-first-example}

With Docker running, clone the regression inputs into a working directory of
your choice and run the small drift example. This step also requires Git
(check with `git --version`). On a Mac, `xcode-select --install` installs the
Command Line Tools, including Git, if needed.

```bash
git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/OPALX-project/regression-tests-x.git
cd regression-tests-x/RegressionTests/Drift-1-fromfile

docker run --rm \
  --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  -v "$PWD:/data" \
  ghcr.io/opalx-project/opalx:cpu Drift-1-fromfile.in --info 2
```

The checkout contains both `Drift-1-fromfile.in` and its required particle
distribution, `distr-gauss.txt`. The run writes results, including
`Drift-1-fromfile.stat`, beside the input. Check that OPALX exits successfully
and the statistics file is present. This is a first-run check; it does not
automatically compare numerical results with the regression references.
See [Run a First Simulation](first-simulation.qmd#regression-smoke-test) for
more about the example and its outputs.

### Run your own simulation {#run-a-simulation}

In Terminal, change to the directory containing your input file, replacing
`/path/to/simulation` and `case.in` with your own directory and filename:

```bash
cd /path/to/simulation

docker run --rm \
  --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 \
  -v "$PWD:/data" \
  ghcr.io/opalx-project/opalx:cpu case.in --info 2
```

The mounted directory is `/data` inside the container and is its working
directory. Output files appear beside your input and belong to your macOS
user. Distribution files, field maps, and other referenced files must be
inside this directory or its subdirectories; use paths relative to the input
working directory. `--rm` removes the container after it exits and keeps the
files written into the mounted directory.

This command uses one MPI rank and four OpenMP threads. Adjust
`OMP_NUM_THREADS` to the CPUs available to Docker.

For multiple MPI ranks, set `OPALX_NP` and increase shared memory, for example:

```bash
docker run --rm \
  --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e OPALX_NP=2 -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 \
  --shm-size=1g \
  -v "$PWD:/data" \
  ghcr.io/opalx-project/opalx:cpu case.in --info 2
```

This requests two ranks with two threads each. Choose shared memory and total
memory to suit the case. Random particle generation draws samples per thread,
so changing the thread count can change the particle sample.

### Image versions

The `cpu` and `latest` tags follow successful builds of `master`; they are
moving development versions, rather than the OPALX 1.0.0 release used in the
source-build instructions below. Run `docker pull` again to obtain an update.
Record the image digest printed by `docker pull` for reproducible runs, and
use `ghcr.io/opalx-project/opalx@sha256:<digest>` in place of the tagged image
to select that exact image. Replace `<digest>` with the recorded hash.

The [Docker README]({{< meta source-code-url >}}/blob/master/docker/README.md)
describes commit and release tags, local image builds, and the development
container.
:::

## Source-build prerequisites

OPALX uses CMake and Kokkos to select the execution backend. The following
toolchain is recommended for current development and production builds:

| Dependency | Recommended version | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| GCC | 13 | Use the same host compiler throughout the dependency stack. |
| Fortran compiler | e.g. gfortran from GCC 13 | Required to build the fetched BLAS/LAPACK dependency. |
| OpenMPI | 4 or 5 | Either major version is suitable; use the MPI wrappers from the selected installation. |
| CUDA | 12.9 | Required only for NVIDIA GPU builds. Match the architecture setting to the target GPU. |
| CMake | 3.24 or newer | OPALX currently declares CMake 3.24 as its minimum version. |
| Git | Recent release | Used to clone OPALX and fetched dependencies. |

These are recommended versions, not a promise that every other combination is
unsupported. Accelerator builds need the matching CUDA or HIP toolchain. Other
core dependencies are obtained by the build unless installed-dependency
options are selected.

On a module-based system, a typical environment is:

```bash
module load gcc/13
module load openmpi/5  # openmpi/4 is also supported
module load cuda/12.9  # CUDA builds only
```

Module names vary between clusters. After loading them, check that `gcc`,
`mpicxx`, and `nvcc` resolve to the intended installations before configuring
the build.

## Clone the source

```bash
git clone --branch OPALX-1.0.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/OPALX-project/OPALX.git
cd OPALX
```

This checks out the **OPALX 1.0.0 release**, whose Git tag is
`OPALX-1.0.0`, in detached-HEAD state. All build commands below use this
checkout. To confirm the selected release, run:

```bash
git describe --tags --exact-match
# Expected: OPALX-1.0.0
```

For ongoing development, clone the default branch separately rather than
reusing a release build directory.


## Configure a CPU build

For a portable single-threaded backend:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build_serial \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DPLATFORMS=SERIAL
cmake --build build_serial -j 8
```

For OpenMP, use a separate build directory:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build_openmp \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DPLATFORMS=OPENMP
cmake --build build_openmp -j 8
```

## Configure a GPU build

An NVIDIA A100 build uses the CUDA backend and Ampere architecture:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build_cuda \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DPLATFORMS=CUDA \
  -DARCH=AMPERE80
cmake --build build_cuda -j 8
```

Select the architecture that matches the target GPU. HIP builds use
`-DPLATFORMS=HIP` and the corresponding AMD architecture.

## Enable tests

To build and run the unit tests for the serial backend:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build_serial \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DPLATFORMS=SERIAL \
  -DOPALX_ENABLE_UNIT_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build_serial -j 8
ctest --test-dir build_serial --output-on-failure
```

For a small end-to-end check of the executable, run the regression input in
[Run a First Simulation](first-simulation.qmd#regression-smoke-test). Unit tests
and simulation regression checks serve different purposes.


See [Build, Test, and CI](../developer-guide/build-test-ci.qmd) for the full
developer workflow and [Configuration Reference](../reference/configuration.qmd)
for the maintained build options.
